The driver's account

Saturday night the CTE into town is always jammed near Chin Swee. I went by Newton and Kim Seng to avoid it. It was faster for the passenger.

  • draft 2 (sampled, sides DRIVER_ADVOCATE, RIDER_ADVOCATE): Partial refund PARTIAL_REFUND, amount SGD 7.45, driver none, confidence 0.85
  • draft 3 (sampled, sides DRIVER_ADVOCATE, RIDER_ADVOCATE): Sent to a human reviewer ESCALATE, amount none, driver none, confidence 0.3

Each draft's own explanation

To the rider and the driver. 1. THE ROUTE. On Saturday 18 July 2026 the trip from Blk 226 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3 to One Raffles Place was driven 17.57 km against the booked optimal route of 14.0 km (trip record EV-TRIP-00107). The excess is 3.57 km — 25.5% of the optimal route. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is established. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (under 50% and under 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 profile check does not run and no driver-conduct referral is made: deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 619 completed trips in 90 days is no pattern. 2. THE GPS TRACE (EV-GPS-00107). It is down-weighted to 0.30 by the pre-pass with issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED — a 331.8 m multipath jump at 21:44:57 near Raffles Place implying impossible speeds. It is NOT impaired for policy: POL-RD-07 asks for a gap over 90 s, a jump over 500 m or a sustained interval over 30 s, and none is present (no gaps; largest jump 331.8 m; 10 s sampling). Both things are true at once — a schema-level impairment and a policy-level clearance are different — so the trace may establish the deviation, and this ruling carries the discount as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. 3. THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic advisory naming a road the optimal route uses, with a validity window overlapping the trip. No advisory is on file — EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — and the driver cites no advisory identifier. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged, and the ruling records that no advisory was on file. POL-RD-04 does not excuse the detour either: no rider message requested one, both waypoint_hint fields are null, and the rider's 21:26 message challenged the route rather than asking for it. No part of the excess is excused. 4. THE REFUND (POL-RD-02; the fare is METERED). recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 14.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.35 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 29.177. charged_total = 36.60. Refund = 36.60 - 29.177 = 7.423, rounded UP to SGD 7.45. There is no ERP, toll, surcharge, waiting fee or promo to add. 7.45 is 20.3% of the charge, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the 90% that would make it a full refund, and it is far above the 0.50 de minimis. 5. CONFIDENCE AND INDEPENDENCE. The excess is carried by the impaired trace at 0.30. The billed distance on EV-FARE-00107 (17.60 km) and the trip record's actual_distance_km (17.60 km) are rounded copies of that same trace measurement, not independent carriers (POL-RD-01, POL-RD-07(ii)), so they do not lift the cap — the argument that the fare ledger is an independent record is rejected. But the deviation is independently carried by the chat log EV-CHAT-00107 (weight 1.0), a contemporaneous record made from inside the trip (the rider's 21:26 objection that the driver had exited at Whitley and the driver's reply), and the driver's own statement admits the route via Newton and Kim Seng — that admission supplies the corroboration POL-RD-08 requires against the rider's claim history, but carrying no weight_multiplier it enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the cap. Two independent artifacts carry the fact, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is their maximum, 1.00, and the 0.70 floor is not breached. Confidence 0.85. 6. RESULT. SGD 7.45 is refunded to the rider. No driver compensation arises: the billed 17.60 km does not fall short of the trace, so the POL-RD-04 compensation limb has no application. No referral arises: there is no phantom gantry or surcharge line (POL-RD-09(4) not engaged) and the deviation is not material (POL-RD-06(c) not engaged). The monetary effect (7.45) is at or below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it is executed on issue. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.
Ruling on trip TRP-00107 (Ang Mo Kio to One Raffles Place, 18 July 2026), for both parties. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. 1. A deviation is established. The trip record EV-TRIP-00107 states the booked optimal route as 14.0 km / 24 min. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00107 measures the route actually driven at 17.57 km. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one and treats the trip record's 17.6 km as a rounded copy of it. The excess is 3.57 km, 25.5% of the optimal, and so passes both POL-RD-01 gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%). It is not a MATERIAL deviation (under 50% and under 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06's uplift and its driver-conduct referral do not arise; the driver's own trailing-90-day figures (deviation_flags_90d 1 of completed_trips_90d 619) would not meet that clause's pattern test in any event, and its lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field it names. 2. The driver's traffic excuse fails. The driver says the CTE was jammed near Chin Swee and that he went by Newton and Kim Seng (counterparty statement; chat EV-CHAT-00107 at 21:26). POL-RD-03 exonerates only on a traffic_advisory that names the road, carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace puts the vehicle there, and is matched by a route leaving and rejoining the corridor. No such advisory exists: EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and the driver names no advisory identifier. Under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight, reduces no excess and supplies no adjusted route, and under POL-RD-13(1) the absent advisory is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The assertion is discarded; no advisory was on file. 3. No rider-requested detour. The chat log holds exactly two messages; neither requests a stop or a route and both waypoint_hint fields are null. The rider challenged the Whitley exit at 21:26, she did not authorise it. POL-RD-04 does not apply and no distance is excluded. 4. The GPS trace is schema-impaired but policy-clean, and both must be said. EV-GPS-00107 carries the pre-pass issues GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED (a 331.8 m multipath jump at 21:44:57 in the Raffles Place urban canyon, implying impossible speeds) and a weight_multiplier of 0.30, which POL-GEN-02(3) requires me to name. For policy purposes under POL-RD-07 it is clean: no gap over 90 s (largest gap 0.0 s), no jump over 500 m (largest 331.8 m), no sampling interval over 30 s (10 s). POL-RD-07's consequences and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged, the deviation may be established on the trace, and the finding survives the 0.30 discount. 5. Confidence. A 0.30 weight would cap confidence if the trace were the only carrier of the deciding fact. It is not. The chat log EV-CHAT-00107 (weight 1.0) is a contemporaneous record made from inside the disputed window and independently supports the deviation, and the driver's own account concedes the route. POL-GEN-02(2) takes the MAXIMUM where independent artifacts carry the fact, so the cap is 1.00, not 0.30, and POL-RD-10(1) is not triggered. I do not rely on the fare breakdown's 17.60 km (called 'an independent billing record' in its admissibility note) or on the trip record's 17.6 km: under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-07(ii) each is a copy of the same trace measurement and corroborates nothing. That argument of the rider's fails in its reasoning even though the no-escalation outcome it seeks is right. 6. The refund (POL-RD-02). fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35 + 0.80 = 29.177. charged_total = 36.60. Refund = 36.60 - 29.177 = 7.423, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 7.45. The 1.35 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is kept. There is no ERP (0.00), no fixed surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo discount. 7.45 is 20.3% of the charge: above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 7.45, not the SGD 12.00 claimed. 7. Burden and profiles. The rider's counters deviation_claims_60d (5) and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated (1), with an excess below 30%, make POL-RD-08 require corroboration beyond the trace; that corroboration is supplied by the driver's own statement admitting the route, one of the sources POL-RD-07(ii) names, so the claim is proven and her history is not used to deny it. Every other profile field (rating, lifetime counters, cancellation rates, prior flags) is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is used for nothing. 8. Effect. The monetary effect (SGD 7.45) does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and is executed on issue under POL-GEN-05. If either party can add a record-type artifact - for example a traffic advisory for the CTE covering 21:13-21:47 on 18 July - POL-GEN-04 allows one appeal within 30 days.
An automated money ruling cannot issue on this record. The case goes to a human reviewer and the $12.00 you are disputing is HELD — not collected, not refunded. 1) The deviation is ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 measures it on the GPS trace: 17.57 km driven against the booked optimal route of 14.0 km, an excess of 3.57 km, which is 25.5% of the optimal route. Both gates are passed (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%). The rider's distance claim is accepted. 2) The trace must be described both ways, and both are true. EV-GPS-00107 is IMPAIRED at the schema level: weight_multiplier 0.30, issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED (a 331.8 m multipath jump at 21:44:57 near Raffles Place, implying 193.6 kph in and 238.9 kph out of the outlier). For POLICY it is clean: none of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is met — no gap over 90 s (largest gap 0.0 s), no jump over 500 m (largest 331.8 m), no sampling interval over 30 s (10 s). So a deviation may be established on the trace, and POL-RD-10(3) is NOT triggered. The driver's disclosure on this point is accepted. 3) Why no refund issues today. POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the lowest weight among the artifacts that carry the deciding fact. The deciding fact is the distance actually driven, and it is carried by the trace at 0.30. The rider's argument that the fare_breakdown (17.60 km billed) and the trip_record (17.6 km) lift the cap to 1.00 is REJECTED: both are copies of the same trace measurement. POL-RD-01 states that trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy that may NOT be cited for the threshold test, and POL-RD-07(ii) states that the billed distance is not independent corroboration where it copies the trace figure. A trip record and a fare ledger computed from the same trace corroborate nothing, so there is no second independent carrier and no maximum to take. The cap is 0.30, below the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation. 4) The arithmetic, on the record (no amount issues while escalated). Reading the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.35): recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + 0.80 platform fee = 29.177. charged_total = 36.60. Refund = 36.60 - 29.177 = 7.423, rounded up to 7.45. That would be a PARTIAL_REFUND, above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share, and at 7.45 it would fall below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and execute automatically. It cannot issue while the confidence cap forces escalation. The rider's refund and non-full-refund claims are therefore noted but cannot be given effect. 5) The driver's traffic explanation is DISCARDED. No traffic advisory is on file — EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, and no congestion advisory was issued for the CTE that evening — so POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13(2) the assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an adjusted optimal route. Because no advisory identifier was cited by the driver, POL-RD-13(1) applies and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. 6) No rider instruction excuses any part of the excess. POL-RD-04 is not met: the chat log holds only the rider's real-time challenge ('why exit at whitley? CTE goes straight down what') and the driver's reply, both with waypoint_hint null. The rider's no-exoneration claim is accepted. The driver's own statement admits the route (Newton and Kim Seng), which satisfies the POL-RD-08 corroboration limb for an excess below 30%, but it carries no weight_multiplier and cannot lift the POL-GEN-02(2) cap. 7) What would resolve this. A reviewer needs one genuinely independent record of the distance driven — for example an ERP gantry record, or another source of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) lists, that places the vehicle on the Newton/Kim Seng corridor independently of this trace — or a human check that the trace's single drift outlier does not affect the measured distance. No clause-mandated referral arises: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review does not fire (deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 619 completed trips in 90 days; no pattern), and POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity does not fire (no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge).
To both parties — this dispute cannot be decided automatically. It goes to a human reviewer and the $36.60 charge is held (neither collected nor refunded) until that review, because POL-RD-10(1) applies: my confidence in any ruling is capped below the 0.70 floor. On the merits, the deviation is real. The governing measurement is the GPS trace: 17.57 km driven against the booked optimal route of 14.0 km, an excess of 3.57 km — 25.5% — past both POL-RD-01 gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%). The driver's own account confirms the route ('I went by Newton and Kim Seng'), and the rider never asked for it: the chat log shows her challenging the route at 21:26, not requesting a detour, so POL-RD-04 exonerates nothing (both waypoint_hint fields are null, so no waypoint test can even be run). The driver's traffic excuse ('CTE very jam tonight boss') names no advisory, and no congestion advisory was on file for that evening — EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so under POL-RD-13(2) it neither reduces the excess nor triggers an escalation. The difficulty is the artifact that carries the distance. EV-GPS-00107 was down-weighted by the admissibility pre-pass to 0.30, with issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED (a 331.8 m multipath jump on the Raffles Place approach implying impossible speeds). It is schema-impaired but NOT impaired for policy: there is no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval over 30 s, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) do not fire and the deviation may still be established on it. Both things are true and I say both. The 17.60 km billed on the fare breakdown and the trip record's actual_distance_km are not independent of that trace — they are rounded copies of the same measurement, so they cannot corroborate it or lift the confidence cap. The driver's statement supports the route, but a counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier and enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the cap. The deciding fact — the excess — therefore rests on EV-GPS-00107 alone at weight 0.30, and under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence cannot exceed 0.30, which is below the 0.70 platform floor. For transparency, had the trace carried the finding at full weight the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would have been a partial refund: charged_total $36.60; recomputed_fare $29.18 = ((3.80 + 0.75×14.0 + 0.28×24.0) × 1.35 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier — not from the trip record, which does not carry the field — + $0.80 platform fee); refund $7.42, rounded up to $7.45. That is 20.3% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share, and above the $0.50 de minimis, so it would have been PARTIAL_REFUND rather than FULL_REFUND or NO_ACTION. The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. No ERP, toll, surcharge, waiting fee or promo applies, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing. No POL-RD-06 pattern arises: the excess is not material (25.5% is under 50% and 3.57 km under 8.0 km), and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 over 619 trips, far under the clause's tests. On the rider profile (deviation_claims_60d 5, substantiated 1), the excess below 30% does require corroboration beyond the trace under POL-RD-08; that is met by the driver's admission of the route, and the factor may never be used to deny an otherwise-proven claim. It does not, however, change the confidence cap. What would resolve this: an independent record of the distance driven that the platform can show is not derived from this trace — a GPS export or a billing statement — so the excess can rest on full-weight evidence. That is a question for the reviewer and is stated here; no clause of the policy produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty.

No such advisory is on file: EV-ADVIS-00107-01 has status MISSING and weight 0.0, and the pre-pass note records that no congestion advisory was issued for the CTE on 18 July 2026. POL-RD-13(1) is express: where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory, the absent artifact is not an exculpatory clause 'invoked against a cited artifact' within POL-RD-10(5) — an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one — and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. The driver's chat reply ('cte very jam tonight boss') and his counterparty statement name no advisory identifier at all. CTE goes straight down what' — and the driver's reply; both waypoint_hint fields are null, the rider asked for no stop and named no alternative route. The charge is still recorded as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, so the present state stands unless and until a ruling moves it — and it should move: $7.45 of the $36.60 is money the rider paid for 3.57 km of detour she did not ask for. The contested $12.00 is not met in full, because the recomputed fare correctly keeps the 1.35 surge multiplier she was charged; I do not ask the judge to strip out surge that the fare_breakdown records. The monetary effect is under the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it should be executed on issue. KEPT; The ruling need not be escalated for want of confidence. But the discount is real, and any ruling that uses this trace must state the artifact, its weight and its issue codes, and say whether the finding survives the discount. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, because that field is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement; POL-RD-07(ii) likewise treats a billed distance derived from the same trace as no independent corroboration. A deciding fact carried by a sole artifact at weight 0.30 caps the Judge's confidence at 0.30 under POL-GEN-02(2), which is below the 0.70 platform-wide floor, so POL-RD-10(1) requires ESCALATE and the contested charge is held rather than refunded. The profile check the clause would require does not help the rider either — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 619, a ratio of 0.0016, nowhere near the 3-flag or 0.05 pattern test — and prior_deviation_flags, being a lifetime counter, is not the field POL-RD-06 asks for. The rider has produced no independent artifact that measures the excess. DISCARDED; If the case is not escalated, the driver's exposure is arithmetic and no more. Nothing in POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 or POL-RD-06 adds to that figure on this record, and no driver compensation arises on the POL-RD-04 limb because the billed distance of 17.60 km exceeds, rather than falls short of, the trace distance.
